questions.text:
निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए तथा उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए :
(i) रूस की क्रान्ति
(ii) अफगानिस्तान पर सोवियत आक्रमण
(iii) सोवियत संघ का विघटन
(iv) द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध का अन्त
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in chronological order and choose the correct option as answer:
(i) The Russian Revolution
(ii) The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
(iii) The disintegration of Soviet Union
(iv) The end of the World War II
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is (D): (i), (iv), (ii), (iii). The Russian Revolution occurred in 1917, the end of World War II was in 1945, the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan took place in 1979, and the disintegration of the Soviet Union happened in 1991. Options A and B are incorrect as they place the Soviet invasion before the end of World War II. Option C is wrong because it places the Soviet disintegration before the invasion of Afghanistan.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम है (D): (i), (iv), (ii), (iii)। रूस की क्रान्ति 1917 में, द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध का अन्त 1945 में, अफगानिस्तान पर सोवियत आक्रमण 1979 में और सोवियत संघ का विघटन 1991 में हुआ था।

questions.text: कौन से मध्य एशियाई देश ने 2001 तक दस वर्ष गृह युद्ध का सामना किया ?
questions.text_english: Which Central Asian Republic witnessed a civil war for ten years till 2001 ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Tajikistan. After the disintegration of the Soviet Union, Tajikistan experienced a prolonged civil war that lasted approximately ten years from 1991 to 2001, involving various political and ethnic factions. Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Azerbaijan did not experience such prolonged civil wars during this period.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) ताजिकिस्तान है। सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद ताजिकिस्तान में लगभग 1991 से 2001 तक दस वर्षीय गृह युद्ध चला। कजाखस्तान, उज्बेकिस्तान और अज़रबैजान में ऐसा लंबा गृह युद्ध नहीं हुआ।

questions.text: जब कोई देश अपने शत्रुओं के साथ अपने विचार और जानकारी साझा करता है तो इस प्रक्रिया को क्या कहते है ?
questions.text_english: A process in which the countries share ideas and information with their rivals is called _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Confidence Building. Confidence Building Measures (CBMs) refer to processes where rival states share ideas, information, and engage in transparency measures to reduce mutual suspicion and the risk of conflict. Alliance Building involves forming formal partnerships, Arms Control deals with limiting weapons, and Balance of Power refers to preventing any one state from dominating others — none of which involves information sharing with rivals.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) विश्वास बहाली है। विश्वास बहाली उपाय (CBMs) वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें प्रतिद्वंद्वी देश एक-दूसरे के साथ विचार और जानकारी साझा करके आपसी संदेह और संघर्ष के जोखिम को कम करते हैं।

questions.text: अच्छे आर्थिक अवसरों की तलाश में, प्रवास करने वाले लोगों को निम्नलिखित में से क्या कहा जाता है ?
questions.text_english: People who seek better economic opportunities abroad are called _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Migrants. Migrants are people who move from one place to another, primarily in search of better economic opportunities and livelihoods. Immigrants specifically refers to people who arrive in a new country permanently, Refugees are those who flee due to persecution or conflict, and Non-Residents simply denotes those living outside their home country, not specifically for economic reasons.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) प्रवासी है। प्रवासी वे लोग होते हैं जो बेहतर आर्थिक अवसरों की तलाश में एक स्थान से दूसरे स्थान पर जाते हैं। शरणार्थी उत्पीड़न के कारण भागते हैं और आप्रवासी स्थायी रूप से नए देश में आते हैं।

questions.text: सूची-I का सूची-II से सही मिलान कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Match the List-I correctly with List-II:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i. The Antarctic Treaty was signed in 1959 (iv), the Montreal Protocol was adopted in 1987 (iii) to address ozone depletion, the Antarctic Environmental Protocol was signed in 1991 (ii), and the Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997 (i) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. All other options incorrectly pair these agreements with their respective years.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है: a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i। अंटार्कटिका संधि 1959 में, मांट्रियल प्रोटोकॉल 1987 में, अंटार्कटिका पर्यावरण प्रोटोकॉल 1991 में और क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल 1997 में हस्ताक्षरित हुए।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में दो कथन दिए गए हैं जिनमें से एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। इन कथनों को ध्यान से पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए :
अभिकथन (A) : भारत, चीन और अन्य विकासशील देशों को क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल की बाध्यताओं से छूट दी गई थी।
कारण (R) : औद्योगिकीकरण के दौरान इन देशों में ग्रीनहाउस गैसों का उत्सर्जन कुछ खास नहीं था।
questions.text_english:
In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the appropriate option as the answer.
Assertion (A) : India, China and other developing countries were exempted from the requirements of Kyoto Protocol.
Reason (R) : Their contribution to the emission of green house gases during the industrialisation period was not significant.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है और कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है और कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. India, China and other developing nations were indeed exempted from the binding emission reduction targets of the Kyoto Protocol because their historical greenhouse gas emissions during the industrialisation period were far less significant compared to developed nations like the USA and European countries, who were the primary contributors to accumulated emissions.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। विकसित देशों के मुकाबले भारत, चीन और विकासशील देशों का औद्योगिकीकरण के दौरान ग्रीनहाउस गैसों में योगदान बहुत कम था, इसलिए उन्हें क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल की बाध्यताओं से छूट दी गई।

questions.text: भारत के किस राज्य में कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी को भारत में पहली बार लोकतांत्रिक चुनावों के माध्यम से सता प्राप्त हुई ?
questions.text_english: For the first time the communist party came to power through democratic elections in which state of India ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Kerala. In 1957, the Communist Party of India (CPI) won the Kerala state assembly elections under E.M.S. Namboodiripad and formed the government, marking the first time in the world that a communist party came to power through free and fair democratic elections. West Bengal and Tripura had communist governments later, and Manipur never had one.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) केरल है। 1957 में ई.एम.एस. नंबूदरीपाद के नेतृत्व में भारतीय कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी ने केरल विधानसभा चुनाव जीता और सरकार बनाई। यह विश्व में पहली बार था जब कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी लोकतांत्रिक चुनावों के माध्यम से सत्ता में आई।
questions.topic: First General Elections and Kerala Communist Government

questions.text: भारत का प्रथम मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त कौन था ?
questions.text_english: The first Chief Election Commissioner of India was _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Sukumar Sen. Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India, serving from 1950 to 1958. He successfully conducted India's first two general elections in 1951-52 and 1957. S.L. Shakdhar, K.V.K. Sundaram, and R.K. Trivedi served in later years as Chief Election Commissioners.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) सुकुमार सेन है। सुकुमार सेन भारत के प्रथम मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त थे जिन्होंने 1950 से 1958 तक सेवा की। उन्होंने 1951-52 और 1957 में भारत के प्रथम दो आम चुनाव सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न कराए।

questions.text: चीन ने किस वर्ष तिब्बत पर कब्जा कर लिया था ?
questions.text_english: In which year did China annex Tibet ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1950. China annexed Tibet in 1950 when the People's Liberation Army entered the region. This annexation was a source of tension between India and China, as India had traditional ties with Tibet. The year 1954 is associated with the Panchsheel Agreement, 1962 was the year of the India-China war, making options B, C, and D incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) 1950 है। चीन ने 1950 में तिब्बत पर कब्जा किया जब पीपुल्स लिबरेशन आर्मी ने वहाँ प्रवेश किया। 1954 पंचशील समझौते का वर्ष था और 1962 भारत-चीन युद्ध का।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में दो कथन दिए गए हैं जिनमें से एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। इन कथनों को ध्यान से पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए :
अभिकथन (A) : मिज़ो नेशनल फ्रंट (MNF) ने स्वतंत्रता के लिए सशस्त्र अभियान शुरू किया था।
कारण (R) : स्वतंत्रता के बाद मिज़ो पहाड़ी क्षेत्र को असम के अन्तर्गत एक स्वायत जिला बनाया गया था।
questions.text_english:
In the following question, Statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a Statement of Reason (R). Choose the appropriate option as the answer.
Assertion (A) : The Mizo National Front (MNF) started an armed campaign for independence.
Reason (R) : After independence the Mizo Hill area was made an autonomous district within Assam.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है और कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है और कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both the Assertion and Reason are correct, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. It is true that the MNF launched an armed campaign for independence, and it is also true that the Mizo Hill area was made an autonomous district within Assam after independence. However, the MNF's armed struggle was primarily triggered by the government's inadequate response to the devastating Mautam famine of 1959, not merely because of its status as an autonomous district. Therefore, the Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। MNF का सशस्त्र अभियान मुख्यतः 1959 के मौताम अकाल के प्रति सरकार की उपेक्षापूर्ण प्रतिक्रिया से उत्पन्न हुआ था, न कि केवल स्वायत जिले की स्थिति के कारण।
questions.chapter: Challenges to and Restoration of Congress System / Regional Aspirations

questions.text: भारत ने निम्नलिखित में से किस औपनिवेशिक शासन से इण्डोनेशिया की शीघ्र स्वतंत्रता के लिए भरपूर प्रयास किए थे ?
questions.text_english: India made earnest effort for the early realisation of freedom of Indonesia from the colonial regime of the _______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Dutch. Indonesia was a colony of the Netherlands (Dutch). India strongly supported Indonesian independence and even refused landing rights to Dutch aircraft during the Dutch military action against Indonesia in 1947. This was a significant example of India's anti-colonial foreign policy under Nehru. Indonesia was not under British, French, or Portuguese colonial rule.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) डच है। इंडोनेशिया नीदरलैंड (डच) का उपनिवेश था। भारत ने इंडोनेशिया की स्वतंत्रता का जोरदार समर्थन किया और 1947 में डच सैन्य कार्रवाई के दौरान डच विमानों को उतरने की अनुमति देने से भी मना कर दिया।

questions.text: भारत के किस राज्य से 'करबी' समुदाय का सम्बन्ध है ?
questions.text_english: 'Karbis' community belongs to which State of India ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Assam. The Karbi community is an indigenous tribal group primarily found in the Karbi Anglong district of Assam. They have historically sought greater autonomy and their own state, making Assam the correct answer. The Karbis are not predominantly associated with Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, or Nagaland.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) असम है। करबी समुदाय मुख्यतः असम के करबी आंगलांग जिले में निवास करने वाला जनजातीय समूह है। इन्होंने अधिक स्वायत्तता और अलग राज्य की मांग की है।
questions.topic: Ethnic Communities and Regional Aspirations in Northeast India

questions.text: पूर्वी पाकिस्तान के लोगों ने किस कारण पश्चिमी पाकिस्तान के प्रभुत्व का विरोध किया ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Why did the people of East Pakistan resent the domination of West Pakistan ? Explain the reason.

key_points: West Pakistan dominated political power and the military, sidelining East Pakistan.
Urdu was imposed as the national language, disregarding Bengali, which was the language of the majority in East Pakistan.
Economic resources and development funds were disproportionately allocated to West Pakistan.

questions.solution: The people of East Pakistan resented the domination of West Pakistan for several important reasons. Politically, West Pakistan controlled the central government and military, leaving East Pakistanis with little representation or power. Economically, the revenue generated from East Pakistan through jute exports was largely spent on the development of West Pakistan. Most significantly, the imposition of Urdu as the sole national language was deeply offensive to the Bengali-speaking population of East Pakistan, who saw it as an attack on their cultural identity. This linguistic and cultural suppression, combined with political marginalisation and economic exploitation, fuelled a strong movement for autonomy that eventually led to the creation of Bangladesh in 1971.
questions.solution_hindi: पूर्वी पाकिस्तान के लोगों ने पश्चिमी पाकिस्तान के प्रभुत्व का विरोध कई कारणों से किया। राजनीतिक रूप से, केंद्र सरकार और सेना पर पश्चिम पाकिस्तान का वर्चस्व था। आर्थिक रूप से, पूर्वी पाकिस्तान की जूट निर्यात से अर्जित आय का अधिकांश हिस्सा पश्चिम पाकिस्तान के विकास में खर्च होता था। सबसे बड़ा कारण था कि उर्दू को एकमात्र राष्ट्रभाषा बनाने से बंगाली भाषा और संस्कृति को खतरा उत्पन्न हो गया।
questions.topic: Partition of Pakistan and Formation of Bangladesh

questions.text: "आतंकवाद सुरक्षा के लिए एक नया खतरा है।" कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Terrorism is a new threat to security." Support the statement.

key_points: Terrorism involves deliberate attacks on civilians to create fear and advance political goals.
It transcends national boundaries, making it a global security threat.
Events like 9/11 demonstrate terrorism's capacity to destabilise nations and alter international relations.

questions.solution: Terrorism has emerged as a new and serious threat to security in the contemporary world. Unlike traditional military threats between states, terrorism involves organised non-state actors who use violence against civilians to create widespread fear and achieve political objectives. The September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States demonstrated how terrorism can cause massive destruction, destabilise economies, and alter international relations. Terrorism does not respect national boundaries — it operates across countries, making it a global challenge. It threatens not only the physical security of citizens but also democratic institutions, civil liberties, and international peace, thus qualifying as a major new dimension of security threat.
questions.solution_hindi: आतंकवाद समकालीन विश्व में सुरक्षा के लिए एक नई और गंभीर चुनौती बन गया है। राज्यों के बीच पारंपरिक सैन्य खतरों के विपरीत, आतंकवाद नागरिकों पर हमला करके भय फैलाता है और राजनीतिक उद्देश्य प्राप्त करना चाहता है। 9/11 जैसी घटनाओं ने दिखाया कि आतंकवाद अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संबंधों को कैसे बदल सकता है। यह राष्ट्रीय सीमाओं की परवाह किए बिना वैश्विक स्तर पर कार्य करता है।

questions.text: स्वतंत्रता के समय भारत के समक्ष विकास के कौन से दो मॉडल थे ? उनके नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Name the two models of development before India on the eve of independence.

key_points: The Liberal-Capitalist model as followed by the USA and Western countries.
The Socialist model as followed by the Soviet Union.

questions.solution: At the time of independence, India had two major models of development before it. The first was the Liberal-Capitalist model, as practised by the United States and Western European countries, which emphasised private ownership, free markets, and parliamentary democracy. The second was the Socialist model, as followed by the Soviet Union, which stressed state ownership of the means of production, centralised planning, and rapid industrialisation under government direction. India ultimately chose a mixed economy approach, drawing elements from both models, with Jawaharlal Nehru favouring a planned economy with a public sector alongside a democratic framework.
questions.solution_hindi: स्वतंत्रता के समय भारत के सामने दो प्रमुख विकास मॉडल थे। पहला था उदारवादी-पूंजीवादी मॉडल, जैसा अमेरिका और पश्चिमी देशों में था, जिसमें निजी स्वामित्व और बाजार अर्थव्यवस्था पर जोर था। दूसरा था समाजवादी मॉडल, जैसा सोवियत संघ में था, जिसमें राज्य के स्वामित्व और केंद्रीय नियोजन को महत्व दिया गया।

questions.text: सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार के प्रयोग को भारत के लिए क्यों जोखिम भरा और खतरनाक कहा गया ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Why was India's experiment with universal adult franchise described as "bold and risky" ? Explain.

key_points: India had an overwhelming rate of illiteracy at the time of independence, raising doubts about voters' ability to make informed choices.
The scale was unprecedented — over 17 crore voters, making it the largest democratic experiment in history at that time.
Widespread poverty and social divisions raised fears about manipulation of voters.

questions.solution: India's experiment with universal adult franchise was described as bold and risky for several compelling reasons. At the time of independence, India had an extremely high rate of illiteracy — nearly 85% of the population could not read or write — which made many sceptical about whether ordinary citizens could make rational political choices. Additionally, the sheer scale of the exercise was unprecedented, with over 17 crore eligible voters across a vast and diverse country. Deep-rooted poverty, caste divisions, and communal tensions raised genuine fears that voters could be easily manipulated or that elections could lead to instability. Despite these concerns, India successfully held its first general elections in 1951-52, proving doubters wrong.
questions.solution_hindi: सार्वभौमिक वयस्क मताधिकार के प्रयोग को जोखिम भरा इसलिए कहा गया क्योंकि स्वतंत्रता के समय भारत में 85% जनता अशिक्षित थी जिससे यह संदेह था कि वे सही निर्णय ले पाएंगे या नहीं। 17 करोड़ से अधिक मतदाताओं के साथ यह दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा लोकतांत्रिक प्रयोग था। गरीबी, जाति और सांप्रदायिक विभाजन से मतदाताओं के प्रभावित होने का भी भय था।
questions.topic: First General Elections and Universal Adult Franchise

questions.text: पारम्परिक सुरक्षा के एक घटक के रूप में 'शक्ति संतुलन' की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain 'Balance of Power' as a component of traditional security.

key_points: Balance of Power is a situation where no single state becomes powerful enough to dominate others.
States maintain this balance by building military strength, forming alliances, or supporting weaker states against stronger ones.
It is a key tool to prevent war and maintain stability in the international system.

questions.solution: Balance of Power is an important component of traditional security in international relations. It refers to a situation where no single state is allowed to become so powerful that it can dominate and dictate terms to all other states in the international system. Countries maintain this balance through various means such as strengthening their own military capabilities, forming alliances with other nations, or supporting weaker states against powerful aggressors. For example, during the Cold War, smaller nations often aligned with either the USA or the Soviet Union to counterbalance the other superpower. This mechanism is considered essential for maintaining stability and preventing any one power from establishing hegemony over others.
questions.solution_hindi: शक्ति संतुलन पारम्परिक सुरक्षा का एक महत्वपूर्ण घटक है। इसका अर्थ है कि किसी भी एक राज्य को इतना शक्तिशाली नहीं बनने दिया जाए कि वह अन्य सभी राज्यों पर अपना प्रभुत्व स्थापित कर सके। देश अपनी सैन्य शक्ति बढ़ाकर, गठबंधन बनाकर या कमजोर देशों को सहयोग देकर यह संतुलन बनाए रखते हैं।

questions.text: मंडल कमीशन की किन्हीं दो सिफारिशों को उजागर कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two recommendations of the Mandal Commission.

key_points: 27% reservation in central government jobs for Other Backward Classes (OBCs).
27% reservation for OBCs in admissions to central government educational institutions.

questions.solution: The Mandal Commission, formally known as the Second Backward Classes Commission chaired by B.P. Mandal, submitted its report in 1980 with significant recommendations. First, it recommended 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central government services and public sector undertakings, in addition to the existing reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Second, it recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in admissions to central government educational institutions and universities. These recommendations, when implemented by the V.P. Singh government in 1990, led to widespread protests and became one of the most debated policy decisions in post-independence India.
questions.solution_hindi: मंडल आयोग ने 1980 में अपनी रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत की। इसकी पहली सिफारिश थी कि अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग (OBC) को केंद्र सरकार की नौकरियों में 27% आरक्षण दिया जाए। दूसरी सिफारिश थी कि केंद्र सरकार के शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में प्रवेश के लिए OBC को 27% आरक्षण प्रदान किया जाए।
questions.chapter: Challenges to and Restoration of Congress System

questions.text: भारत की स्वतंत्रता के समय, विश्व में उपस्थित चुनौतीपूर्ण और कठिन परिस्थितियों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the challenging and difficult conditions prevailing in the world at the time of India's independence.

key_points: The world was just recovering from the devastation of World War II, with massive destruction and instability.
The Cold War between the USA and the Soviet Union had begun, dividing the world into two hostile blocs.
The process of decolonisation was underway, but newly independent nations faced immense challenges.
The threat of nuclear war loomed large after the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
The United Nations had just been established and the new world order was uncertain and fragile.

questions.solution: When India gained independence in 1947, the world was passing through an extremely challenging and turbulent phase. The Second World War had just ended in 1945, leaving behind massive destruction, economic devastation, and millions of deaths across Europe and Asia. The world was struggling to rebuild itself from this catastrophe. At the same time, the Cold War had begun between the United States and the Soviet Union, dividing the world into two competing ideological blocs — the capitalist West and the communist East. Every newly independent nation was pressured to align with one of these blocs. The use of atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki had introduced the terrifying prospect of nuclear annihilation, creating a permanent atmosphere of fear. The process of decolonisation was underway in Asia and Africa, but it was accompanied by violence, instability, and economic backwardness. The United Nations had just been established in 1945 to maintain international peace, but its effectiveness was uncertain. In this complex global environment, India had to chart its own independent foreign policy path.
questions.solution_hindi: जब भारत को 1947 में स्वतंत्रता मिली, विश्व अत्यंत कठिन और उथल-पुथल भरे दौर से गुज़र रहा था। द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध 1945 में समाप्त हुआ था जिसने यूरोप और एशिया में भारी विनाश किया था। शीत युद्ध का आरंभ हो चुका था और विश्व अमेरिका और सोवियत संघ के नेतृत्व में दो शिविरों में बंट गया था। परमाणु बम की विनाशकारी शक्ति का भय था और नव-स्वतंत्र राष्ट्रों पर किसी एक गुट से जुड़ने का दबाव था। इन जटिल परिस्थितियों में भारत को अपनी स्वतंत्र विदेश नीति का निर्माण करना था।
questions.topic: World Conditions at the Time of India's Independence

questions.text: "शीत युद्ध के अन्त के बाद, भारत ने रूस के साथ अच्छे सम्बन्ध बनाए रखे।" चार उदाहरणों की सहायता से कथन को न्यायसंगत ठहराइये।
questions.text_english: "India has maintained good relations with Russia after the end of Cold War." Justify the statement with four examples.

key_points: India and Russia signed the Indo-Russian Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation in 1971, which continued to influence bilateral ties.
Russia has remained India's largest arms supplier, providing advanced military equipment including fighter jets, submarines, and nuclear reactors.
Both countries cooperate in space exploration through ISRO-Roscosmos collaboration.
India and Russia conduct joint military exercises and share strategic interests regarding multipolarity in international relations.

questions.solution: India and Russia have maintained exceptionally warm and cooperative relations even after the end of the Cold War in 1991, as evidenced by several concrete examples. First, Russia has continued to be India's most significant defence partner, supplying advanced military hardware including MiG and Sukhoi aircraft, T-90 tanks, Akula-class nuclear submarines, and S-400 missile defence systems, making Russia the largest arms exporter to India. Second, the two countries share a vision of a multipolar world order, opposing the dominance of any single power, which aligns their strategic perspectives in international forums like the United Nations. Third, India and Russia cooperate extensively in the field of civilian nuclear energy, with Russia assisting in the construction of nuclear power plants at Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu. Fourth, both countries have enhanced trade, economic ties, and bilateral visits at the highest level, with the Annual India-Russia Summit mechanism being a regular feature of their diplomatic engagement, reflecting the depth and continuity of this strategic partnership.
questions.solution_hindi: शीत युद्ध की समाप्ति के बाद भी भारत और रूस के संबंध मजबूत बने रहे हैं। पहला, रूस भारत का सबसे बड़ा रक्षा साझेदार बना रहा और सुखोई विमान, T-90 टैंक, S-400 मिसाइल प्रणाली और परमाणु पनडुब्बियाँ प्रदान कीं। दूसरा, दोनों देश बहुध्रुवीय विश्व व्यवस्था के समर्थक हैं। तीसरा, रूस ने कुडनकुलम परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्र की स्थापना में भारत की मदद की। चौथा, वार्षिक शिखर सम्मेलन की परंपरा कायम है जो द्विपक्षीय संबंधों की गहराई को दर्शाती है।

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: 1975 में भारत में लगाए गए आपातकाल से सीखे गए किन्हीं दो पाठों (सबकों) को उजागर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Highlight any two lessons learnt from the imposition of Emergency in India in 1975.

key_points: The Emergency demonstrated that democracy cannot be taken for granted and that citizens must remain vigilant against authoritarian tendencies.
It showed that civil liberties and fundamental rights are essential and their suspension harms democracy.
The 1977 election results proved that the Indian electorate was mature and capable of punishing the misuse of power.

sub_questions.solution: The Emergency of 1975-77 imposed by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi taught Indian democracy several enduring lessons. The first major lesson was that democracy is not indestructible and can be subverted by those in power if citizens and institutions are not vigilant. The suspension of fundamental rights, arrest of opposition leaders, and censorship of the press showed how quickly civil liberties can be curtailed. This strengthened the commitment of political parties and citizens to protect constitutional rights. The second important lesson was about the resilience and maturity of the Indian electorate. When the Emergency was lifted and elections were held in 1977, the people of India voted decisively against the Congress Party, removing it from power for the first time since independence. This demonstrated that even an ordinary voter values freedom and democracy deeply, and that democracy ultimately belongs to the people, not to any leader or party.

sub_questions.text: 1975 में भारत में लगाए गए आपातकाल के किन्हीं चार परिणामों को उजागर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Highlight any four consequences of the imposition of Emergency in India in 1975.

key_points: Fundamental rights of citizens were suspended and habeas corpus was not applicable.
Press censorship was imposed and media freedom was curtailed.
Opposition leaders and activists were arrested under MISA (Maintenance of Internal Security Act).
The Emergency ultimately led to the defeat of the Congress Party in the 1977 elections and the formation of the Janata Party government.

sub_questions.solution: The imposition of Emergency in India in 1975 had several significant consequences. First, the fundamental rights of citizens, including the right to personal liberty, were suspended, and the courts were barred from entertaining habeas corpus petitions, leaving citizens without legal protection against arbitrary arrest. Second, hundreds of opposition leaders, activists, and journalists were arrested under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), removing all organised political opposition. Third, strict press censorship was imposed, with newspapers required to submit content for government approval before publication, severely curtailing freedom of the press. Fourth, a forced sterilisation programme was implemented as part of the population control policy, causing widespread resentment especially in North India. Finally, the Emergency contributed to the electoral defeat of the Congress Party in the 1977 general elections, leading to the formation of the Janata Party government under Morarji Desai — the first non-Congress government at the Centre in independent India's history.

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: सांस्कृतिक समरूपता और सांस्कृतिक वैभिन्नीकरण के बीच अन्तर को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the difference between cultural homogenisation and cultural hetrogenisation.

key_points: Cultural homogenisation refers to the process whereby local and diverse cultures are replaced by a single dominant global culture.
Cultural heterogenisation refers to the process where globalisation leads to the creation of new mixed or hybrid cultures rather than erasing local ones.
Homogenisation results in cultural uniformity, often dominated by Western or American culture, while heterogenisation results in cultural diversity and fusion.

sub_questions.solution: Cultural homogenisation and cultural heterogenisation are two contrasting outcomes of globalisation. Cultural homogenisation refers to the process by which the spread of global media, multinational corporations, and technology leads to the replacement of local, diverse cultures by a single dominant culture — usually Western or American culture. This results in the worldwide popularity of similar food, music, clothing, and values, diminishing regional cultural identities. For example, the global spread of fast food chains and Hollywood movies represents cultural homogenisation. Cultural heterogenisation, on the other hand, refers to the process whereby globalisation does not erase local cultures but instead creates new hybrid or mixed cultures by blending global influences with local traditions. Rather than uniformity, it produces cultural diversity and fusion. For instance, the fusion of Western music with Indian classical traditions or the mixing of global fashion trends with local styles represents heterogenisation, resulting in a richer and more diverse cultural landscape.

sub_questions.text: वैश्वीकरण के किन्हीं दो आर्थिक परिणामों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any two economic consequences of globalisation.

key_points: Globalisation has led to increased foreign direct investment (FDI) and economic growth in developing countries.
It has also increased inequality, as the benefits of globalisation are unevenly distributed between developed and developing nations.

sub_questions.solution: Globalisation has had profound economic consequences across the world. The first major economic consequence is the flow of foreign direct investment (FDI) and the expansion of multinational corporations. Globalisation has opened up markets in developing countries, bringing in capital, technology, and employment opportunities. Countries like India and China witnessed significant economic growth due to increased FDI, export-led growth, and integration with the global economy. This led to a rise in GDP, expansion of the middle class, and improved living standards for many people. The second significant economic consequence is the rise in economic inequality. While globalisation has benefited some sections of society, it has also led to the displacement of workers in labour-intensive industries due to automation and competition from cheaper imports. Small-scale industries and farmers in developing countries often cannot compete with multinational corporations, leading to widening gaps between the rich and the poor both within and between nations. Thus, the economic consequences of globalisation are a mix of growth and inequality.

questions.text: भारत ने अपने लोगों की क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाओं का निपटारा किस तरीके से किया है ? किन्हीं दो उदाहरणों की सहायता से स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: How did India address the regional aspirations of the people ? Explain with the help of any two examples.

key_points: India addressed regional aspirations through the reorganisation of states on linguistic lines after the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.
India created new states to meet regional demands, such as Nagaland in 1963, Meghalaya in 1972, and more recently Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Uttarakhand in 2000.
India resolved ethnic conflicts through negotiation and peace accords, such as the Mizoram Peace Accord of 1986.
The federal structure of India allows states autonomy in many matters, accommodating regional aspirations within a unified framework.

questions.solution: India has largely addressed the regional aspirations of its people through peaceful democratic means, accommodation, and constitutional mechanisms rather than outright suppression. The first major example is the reorganisation of states on linguistic lines. After intense agitations, particularly the Andhra movement following the death of Potti Sriramulu in 1952, the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 was passed, redrawing state boundaries primarily on the basis of language. This accommodation of linguistic identities — such as the creation of Andhra Pradesh for Telugu speakers, Maharashtra for Marathi speakers, and Karnataka for Kannada speakers — significantly reduced tensions and gave regional communities a sense of belonging within the Indian Union. The second important example is the Mizoram Peace Accord of 1986. After decades of armed insurgency by the Mizo National Front (MNF) demanding independence, the Indian government under Rajiv Gandhi negotiated a peace agreement with Laldenga, the MNF leader. Mizoram was granted full statehood, and the MNF laid down arms and joined mainstream politics. This demonstrated India's preference for dialogue and accommodation in resolving regional aspirations, transforming a separatist movement into a participant in democratic governance.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत ने अपने लोगों की क्षेत्रीय आकांक्षाओं को मुख्यतः लोकतांत्रिक और संवैधानिक तरीकों से हल किया। पहला उदाहरण है 1956 में भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों का पुनर्गठन। आंध्र आंदोलन के बाद राज्य पुनर्गठन अधिनियम पारित हुआ और भाषाई पहचान के आधार पर नए राज्य बने जिससे क्षेत्रीय तनाव कम हुआ। दूसरा उदाहरण है 1986 का मिजोरम शांति समझौता, जिसमें MNF ने हथियार रखे और मिजोरम को पूर्ण राज्य का दर्जा मिला।

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए अवतरण को ध्यान से पढ़िये और निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए :

वैश्विक राजनीति के अन्तर्गत, पर्यावरणीय मुद्दों पर अधिक ध्यान देने की प्रक्रिया ने ब्राजील के रियो डी जनेरियों में संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ के पर्यावरण और विकास के मुद्दे पर केन्द्रित एक सम्मेलन में ठोस रूप लिया। इसको पृथ्वी-शिखर सम्मेलन भी कहा गया।
questions.text_english:
Read the passage given below carefully and answer the questions that follow:

The growing focus on environmental issues within the arena of global politics was firmly consolidated at United Nations Conference on Environment and Development held in Rio de Janeiro of Brazil. This was also called the Earth Summit.

sub_questions.text: पृथ्वी-शिखर सम्मेलन किस वर्ष हुआ था ?
sub_questions.text_english: In which year was the Earth Summit held ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1992. The Earth Summit, formally known as the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil in June 1992. It was a landmark event in global environmental politics that brought together world leaders to discuss sustainable development.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस देश को क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल की बाध्यताओं से छूट दी गई थी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries was exempted from the requirements of the Kyoto Protocol ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) China. China, along with India and other developing countries, was exempted from the binding emission reduction targets of the Kyoto Protocol because their historical contribution to greenhouse gas emissions during the industrialisation period was considered not significant compared to developed nations. The USA, UK, and France, as developed nations, were subject to the protocol's binding commitments.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प रियो शिखर-सम्मेलन का परिणाम नहीं था ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following was not an outcome of the Rio Summit ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Kyoto Protocol. The Kyoto Protocol was not a direct outcome of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. It was adopted separately in Kyoto, Japan in 1997 at the Third Conference of Parties (COP3). The Rio Summit's actual outcomes included Agenda-21 (a global action plan for sustainable development), the principle of Sustainable Development, and the concept of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR).

sub_questions.text: अस्सी के दशक के मध्य में निम्नलिखित में से किसके ऊपर ओज़ोन परत में छिद्र खोजा गया था ?
sub_questions.text_english: The Ozone hole was discovered in the mid 80's over the _______.
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Antarctic. In the mid-1980s, scientists discovered a significant depletion or 'hole' in the ozone layer over Antarctica. This discovery was a major alarm for the international community, leading to the Montreal Protocol of 1987, which aimed to phase out the use of ozone-depleting substances like CFCs. The ozone hole was not found over the Atlantic Ocean, Pacific Ocean, or Arctic Ocean.

questions.text:
भारत के दिए गए राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र में चार राज्यों को (A), (B), (C) और (D) के द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। नीचे दी गई जानकारी के आधार पर इन राज्यों की पहचान कीजिए और अपनी उत्तर-पुस्तिका में इनके सही नाम, प्रयोग की गई जानकारी की क्रम संख्या तथा मानचित्र में दिया गया संबंधित अक्षर, नीचे दी गई तालिका के रूप में लिखिए :
(i) वह राज्य जिससे कांग्रेस के पूर्व अध्यक्ष के. कामराज का सम्बन्ध था।
(ii) वह राज्य जहाँ से 'आया राम, गया राम' कहावत का जन्म हुआ।
(iii) वह राज्य जिससे पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री लाल बहादुर शास्त्री का सम्बन्ध था।
(iv) वह राज्य जहाँ 1967 के विधान-सभा चुनावों में कांग्रेस पार्टी को बहुमत प्राप्त नहीं हुआ था।
questions.text_english:
In the given outline Map of India, four states have been marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify the States on the basis of the information given below and write their correct names in the answer book alongwith the respective serial numbers of the information used and the concerned alphabet as per the format that follows:
(i) The State to which the former Congress President K. Kamraj belonged.
(ii) The State from where the phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' originated.
(iii) The State to which former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri belonged.
(iv) The State where the Congress Party did not get majority in 1967 assembly elections.

key_points: (i) - C - Tamil Nadu (K. Kamraj was a Congress President and Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu)
(ii) - B - Haryana (The phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' originated in Haryana due to frequent defections)
(iii) - D - Uttar Pradesh (Lal Bahadur Shastri belonged to UP, born in Mughalsarai/Varanasi region)
(iv) - A - Bihar or another state where Congress did not get majority in 1967

questions.solution: Based on the clues provided and the position of the letters on the map: (i) Serial number (i) corresponds to letter C, which is Tamil Nadu. K. Kamraj was a prominent Congress leader and served as President of the Indian National Congress. He was the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu and is closely associated with that state. (ii) Serial number (ii) corresponds to letter B, which is Haryana. The phrase 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' originated in Haryana in 1967 when MLA Gaya Lal switched parties multiple times in a single day, giving rise to this expression for political defection. (iii) Serial number (iii) corresponds to letter D, which is Uttar Pradesh. Former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri was born in Mughalsarai (now Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyay Nagar) in Uttar Pradesh and is closely associated with that state. (iv) Serial number (iv) corresponds to letter A, which is Bihar (or whichever state is marked A on the map where Congress did not get majority in 1967 assembly elections, contributing to the phenomenon of coalition politics).
questions.solution_hindi: (i) क्रम संख्या (i) - अक्षर C - तमिलनाडु: के. कामराज तमिलनाडु के मुख्यमंत्री और कांग्रेस के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष थे। (ii) क्रम संख्या (ii) - अक्षर B - हरियाणा: 'आया राम गया राम' कहावत 1967 में हरियाणा में MLAगया लाल के बार-बार दल बदलने से उत्पन्न हुई। (iii) क्रम संख्या (iii) - अक्षर D - उत्तर प्रदेश: लाल बहादुर शास्त्री मुगलसराय, UP में जन्मे थे। (iv) क्रम संख्या (iv) - अक्षर A - बिहार: 1967 के चुनावों में कांग्रेस को बहुमत नहीं मिला।

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए श्रीलंका से संबंधित कार्टून का अध्ययन कीजिए और निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए :
(i) कार्टून में दिखाया गया 'बाघ' किस समुदाय का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है ?
(ii) कार्टून में दिखाया गया शेर किस समुदाय का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है ?
(iii) राजपक्षे द्वारा सन्तुलन बैठाने के करतब का क्या उद्देश्य है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Study the cartoon given below related to Sri Lanka and answer the questions that follow:
(i) Which community does the tiger shown in the cartoon represent ?
(ii) Which community does the Lion shown in the cartoon represent ?
(iii) What did the balancing act by Rajpakshe aim at ? Explain.

sub_questions.text: कार्टून में दिखाया गया 'बाघ' किस समुदाय का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which community does the tiger shown in the cartoon represent ?

key_points: The tiger represents the Tamil community / LTTE (Tamil Tigers)

sub_questions.solution: The tiger in the cartoon represents the Tamil community, specifically the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), also known as the Tamil Tigers. The tiger was the symbol of the LTTE, which fought for a separate Tamil homeland called Eelam in Sri Lanka.

sub_questions.text: कार्टून में दिखाया गया शेर किस समुदाय का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which community does the Lion shown in the cartoon represent ?

key_points: The lion represents the Sinhalese community / Sinhala majority

sub_questions.solution: The lion in the cartoon represents the Sinhalese community, who form the majority population of Sri Lanka. The lion is the national symbol of Sri Lanka and is closely associated with the Sinhalese Buddhist identity and Sinhala nationalism.

sub_questions.text: राजपक्षे द्वारा सन्तुलन बैठाने के करतब का क्या उद्देश्य है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What did the balancing act by Rajpakshe aim at ? Explain.

key_points: Rajapaksa was trying to balance the competing demands of the Tamil and Sinhalese communities.
He aimed to end the civil war while also satisfying Sinhala nationalist demands, a difficult political balancing act.

sub_questions.solution: The balancing act by Rajapakshe in the cartoon symbolises the difficult political challenge he faced as the President of Sri Lanka. On one side was the LTTE (Tamil Tigers) representing the Tamil community's demand for a separate homeland, and on the other side was the Sinhalese majority community with its own nationalist aspirations. Rajapakshe's balancing act aimed at resolving the long-standing ethnic conflict in Sri Lanka — he ultimately chose a military solution, crushing the LTTE militarily in 2009. The cartoon highlights the political tightrope that Sri Lankan leaders had to walk in managing the ethnic tensions between the Tamil minority and the Sinhala majority while maintaining national unity.

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: यूरोपीय संघ को विश्व का एक प्रभावशाली क्षेत्रीय संगठन बनाने वाले किन्हीं चार कारकों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any four factors that make the European Union an influential regional organisation of the world.

key_points: The EU has a common currency (Euro) used by most member states, giving it significant economic power.
The EU has a large combined GDP, making it one of the world's largest economies.
The EU has a common foreign and security policy, giving it diplomatic clout on the world stage.
The EU has evolved its own institutions like the European Parliament, European Commission, and European Court of Justice.
The EU has a large combined military capability and serves as a major power in NATO.

sub_questions.solution: The European Union (EU) is one of the most influential regional organisations in the world, and several key factors account for its prominence. First, the EU has developed a common currency, the Euro, which is used by most of its member states. This monetary union has created one of the largest economic zones in the world, enabling free trade, greater investment, and economic stability among members. Second, the EU collectively represents the world's largest or second-largest economy by GDP, giving it immense economic bargaining power in international trade negotiations and financial forums. Third, the EU has developed a Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), allowing it to speak with a unified voice on major international issues, making it a significant diplomatic actor capable of influencing global events. Fourth, the EU has established well-functioning supranational institutions — the European Parliament, the European Commission, the Council of the EU, and the European Court of Justice — which allow it to govern across borders and create binding laws applicable to all members. These factors combine to make the EU far more than a simple trade bloc, transforming it into a quasi-federal entity with global influence.

sub_questions.text: क्षेत्रीय संगठनों को स्थापित करने के किन्हीं चार उद्देश्यों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any four objectives of establishing the regional organisations.

key_points: To promote economic cooperation and trade among member nations.
To maintain regional peace and security by providing a forum for dispute resolution.
To collectively represent the interests of member states in international forums.
To promote social, cultural, and political integration among neighbouring countries.

sub_questions.solution: Regional organisations are established with several important objectives that aim to benefit member states collectively. The first and most prominent objective is to promote economic cooperation and free trade. By eliminating trade barriers among member nations, regional organisations create larger markets, attract investment, and stimulate economic growth. ASEAN and SAARC, for example, pursue this objective through free trade agreements. The second objective is to maintain regional peace, security, and stability. Regional organisations provide mechanisms for the peaceful resolution of disputes among member states, preventing conflicts from escalating. The African Union and ASEAN have played important roles in conflict resolution within their respective regions. The third objective is to present a collective voice in international forums. Individually, smaller nations may have limited influence in bodies like the UN or WTO, but as part of a regional bloc they can negotiate more effectively, protect their collective interests, and shape global policies. The fourth objective is to promote social, cultural, and political integration. Regional bodies foster people-to-people contacts, cultural exchanges, and shared educational programmes, creating a sense of regional identity and cooperation that goes beyond merely economic interests. SAARC's cultural programmes and the EU's freedom of movement are examples of this dimension.

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद के संगठन तथा उसे अधिक प्रासंगिक बनाने के लिए प्रस्तावित सुधारों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the composition of the United Nations Security Council and the suggested reforms to make it more relevant.

key_points: The UNSC has 15 members — 5 permanent (P5: USA, UK, France, Russia, China) and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms.
The P5 members have the power of veto.
Reforms suggested include expansion of permanent membership to include countries like India, Germany, Japan, and Brazil.
Reforms also call for limiting or abolishing the veto power to make the Council more democratic.

sub_questions.solution: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) is the most powerful organ of the United Nations, with primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. It is composed of 15 members in total: five permanent members (P5) — the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China — and ten non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms on the basis of regional representation. The most significant feature is the veto power enjoyed by the P5, which means any one permanent member can block any substantive resolution, giving them extraordinary influence over international affairs. This structure reflects the post-World War II global order and is increasingly seen as outdated. Suggested reforms to make the UNSC more relevant and representative include: expanding the number of permanent members to include major powers like India, Germany, Japan, and Brazil (the G4 nations), who argue that they contribute significantly to the UN's budget and peacekeeping operations but have no permanent seat. Reformers also advocate for adding permanent seats for African nations to represent the developing world. Additionally, many nations call for reform or abolition of the veto power, arguing that it enables powerful nations to block action even on clear cases of aggression or human rights violations, as seen in various crises where P5 members have used the veto for national interests rather than global justice.

sub_questions.text: शीत युद्ध की समाप्ति के बाद विश्व राजनीति में आए किन्हीं चार परिवर्तनों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four changes that occurred in world politics after the end of Cold War.

key_points: The collapse of the Soviet Union and the emergence of the United States as the sole superpower (unipolar world).
The emergence of new independent states from the former Soviet Union.
The dominance of market economy and liberal democracy as the accepted global norms.
The rise of new security threats such as terrorism, ethnic conflicts, and nuclear proliferation.

sub_questions.solution: The end of the Cold War in 1991 brought about profound transformations in world politics. The first and most dramatic change was the collapse of the Soviet Union, which led to the emergence of fifteen new independent states including Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, and others. This fundamentally altered the geopolitical map of Eurasia and ended the bipolar world order that had dominated since 1945. The second major change was the emergence of the United States as the sole superpower in a unipolar world. With no rival superpower, the USA gained unprecedented influence over global politics, economics, and military affairs, leading to what some scholars have called the 'unipolar moment.' The third significant change was the global spread of liberal democracy and market capitalism as the dominant ideological framework. With the discrediting of communist planned economies, most countries transitioned towards market economies and multiparty democracy, accelerated by globalisation and the influence of international financial institutions like the IMF and World Bank. The fourth change was the rise of new types of threats to international security, including international terrorism (culminating in the 9/11 attacks), ethnic and civil conflicts within states, nuclear proliferation concerns, and environmental crises. These challenges required new forms of international cooperation beyond the traditional state-centric security framework of the Cold War era.

questions.topic: UNSC Reforms / Changes after Cold War

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: 1947 में ब्रिटिश इण्डिया के विभाजन के किन्हीं चार परिणामों का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any four consequences of the partition of British India in 1947.

key_points: Massive communal violence and riots resulted in hundreds of thousands of deaths.
One of the largest forced migrations in human history — approximately 1.5 crore people were displaced.
Division of assets including the civil services, armed forces, and financial resources between India and Pakistan.
The partition created a lasting hostility between India and Pakistan, leading to multiple wars and ongoing tensions.

sub_questions.solution: The partition of British India in 1947 had devastating and far-reaching consequences. The first and most tragic consequence was the outbreak of widespread communal violence. The drawing of new boundaries in Punjab and Bengal triggered massive riots between Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs, resulting in the deaths of between 2 lakh and 5 lakh people, with some estimates placing the figure even higher. Cities like Lahore, Amritsar, and Calcutta witnessed unprecedented bloodshed. The second consequence was the largest forced migration in recorded human history. Approximately 1.5 crore people were uprooted from their homes — Hindus and Sikhs fleeing Pakistan and Muslims fleeing India — creating a massive refugee crisis that both newly independent nations struggled to manage. The third consequence was the difficult division of administrative and military assets. The Indian Civil Service, armed forces, railways, and financial reserves had to be divided between the two new nations, a process that was deeply contentious and fraught with logistical challenges, weakening both states at the very moment of their birth. The fourth long-term consequence was the creation of a deeply adversarial relationship between India and Pakistan. The circumstances of partition — particularly the communal violence and the unresolved issue of Jammu and Kashmir — planted the seeds of lasting hostility that led to wars in 1947, 1965, 1971, and 1999, and continues to shape South Asian geopolitics to this day.

sub_questions.text: ब्रिटिश इण्डिया के विभाजन की प्रक्रिया के दौरान सामने आई किन्हीं तीन समस्याओं का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three problems that were faced during the process of partition of British India.

key_points: The problem of drawing boundaries: The Radcliffe Line was drawn hastily, dividing communities and families.
The problem of massive communal violence and displacement of millions of people.
The problem of dividing administrative, military, and financial assets between India and Pakistan.

sub_questions.solution: The process of partitioning British India in 1947 was accompanied by several serious and deeply painful problems. The first major problem was the drawing of boundaries. The Radcliffe Commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe who had never visited India before, was given the difficult task of drawing the new international boundary between India and Pakistan in just five weeks. The Radcliffe Line divided the provinces of Punjab and Bengal, splitting communities, families, irrigation canals, and railway lines with little regard for the human cost. Many areas of mixed population were torn apart overnight, creating confusion and resentment. The second major problem was the massive outbreak of communal violence and the resulting refugee crisis. As the boundaries were announced, horrific riots erupted in Punjab and Bengal, with Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs attacking each other. Trains carrying refugees arrived at their destinations filled with dead bodies. The scale of human suffering — deaths, rapes, abductions, and forced conversions — was unimaginable and left deep psychological scars on both nations. The third significant problem was the division of assets and administrative machinery. The two new nations had to divide the financial reserves of the British Indian government, the civil services, the armed forces, railways, post offices, and other infrastructure. This was a logistically nightmarish process conducted under extreme time pressure and communal tension, leaving both India and Pakistan weakened at the very moment they needed strong institutions to cope with the chaos of partition.

questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

sub_questions.text: भारत की अधिकांश राजनीतिक पार्टियों के बीच उभरे सहमति के किन्हीं तीन महत्वपूर्ण मुद्दों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three important issues on which a consensus has emerged among most political parties of India.

key_points: Consensus on New Economic Policy: Most parties accept the broad framework of liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation introduced since 1991.
Consensus on the accommodation of backward castes in government jobs and educational institutions through reservations.
Consensus on the need to decentralise power through Panchayati Raj institutions and strengthen local self-government.
Consensus on the role of the private sector in economic development.

sub_questions.solution: In the era of coalition politics and multi-party competition in India, several important areas of consensus have emerged among most political parties, transcending ideological differences. The first area of consensus is acceptance of the New Economic Policy framework introduced in 1991. While parties may differ in emphasis, virtually all major national and regional parties have accepted the broad framework of economic liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation. Even parties of the left that initially opposed liberalisation have not reversed these policies when in power, indicating a broad political consensus on integrating India into the global economy. The second area of consensus is the policy of affirmative action for socially and educationally backward communities. The implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations and the extension of reservations to Other Backward Classes in government jobs and educational institutions has received broad support across parties, reflecting a shared commitment to social justice and representation for marginalised groups. The third area of consensus is the strengthening of democratic decentralisation. The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies, enjoy broad multi-party support. This consensus recognises that grassroots democracy and empowerment of local governments are essential for effective governance and inclusive development in a country as large and diverse as India.

sub_questions.text: 1989 के बाद भारत में बनी गठबन्धन की सरकारों के किन्हीं तीन लाभों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three benefits of the coalition governments formed in India since 1989.

key_points: Coalition governments have given representation to regional parties and regional aspirations in the central government.
They have promoted greater accommodation of diverse social groups and prevented the dominance of any single party or ideology.
Coalition politics has strengthened federalism by increasing the bargaining power of states vis-a-vis the Centre.

sub_questions.solution: Since 1989, India has been largely governed by coalition governments formed by multiple parties, and this experience has brought several significant benefits to Indian democracy. The first important benefit is that coalition governments have given regional parties a significant voice in national governance. Regional parties representing the aspirations of specific states or communities — such as the Dravida parties of Tamil Nadu, the Trinamool Congress of West Bengal, or the Telugu Desam Party of Andhra Pradesh — have become important partners in central governments. This has ensured that regional concerns, interests, and aspirations are taken into account in national policy-making, promoting a more inclusive and representative form of governance. The second benefit is that coalition governments have promoted greater social diversity in the exercise of political power. With no single party commanding an absolute majority, governments must accommodate the demands of partners representing different castes, communities, religions, and linguistic groups. This has led to greater representation of backward classes, minorities, and regional communities in the cabinet and government, making the system more representative of India's plural society. The third benefit is that coalition politics has significantly strengthened Indian federalism. Regional parties holding the balance of power have successfully demanded greater autonomy, resources, and decision-making authority for states. The increasing devolution of funds to states and the strengthening of the Finance Commission's role can partly be attributed to the bargaining power that regional parties gained through coalition arrangements, making centre-state relations more balanced and cooperative.

questions.topic: Political Consensus and Coalition Governments in India
